title: Verdict and Cipher
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Vane is exhumed for a centennial ceremony and found empty, archivist Hazel Lockridge is pulled from the margins into a murder investigation that threatens to expose her secret history of solving the cathedral's 'accidental' deaths. Her search for the missing witness—rumored to be Vane's illegitimate daughter, declared dead decades ago—leads through forged burial records, a corrupt judge presiding over the coming trial, and a love she must weigh against her duty to the truth. In the end, Hazel finds the witness alive in hiding, chooses justice outside the law by testifying through an anonymous affidavit that topples the judge, and finally claims her own name and identity in the town she once haunted invisibly.
about_author: Lena Okonkwo is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, deaths, and quiet scandals before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people history overlooked, drawing on her fascination with archives as places where truth waits patiently to be found.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Stone
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On the morning of the founder's centennial exhumation, Hazel catalogs the crypt's records and notices an anomaly in Vane's burial ledger—a second entry, inked decades later. When the coffin is opened before the gathered town, it holds only river stones. The beat: dread beneath routine, the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with flashbacks. Detective Ivo Marsh confronts her after realizing three past 'accidents' match patterns she'd flagged privately in the archive. Forced to reveal her unofficial investigations, she bargains: help her find the missing witness, and she'll share everything. The beat: reluctant alliance, pride wounded, curiosity ignited.

chapters.title: The Daughter Nobody Buried
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Digging into Vane's will, Hazel uncovers references to 'M.C.,' a daughter erased from every public record yet paid an annuity until twenty years ago—the year the payments stopped and the first 'accident' occurred. The beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by fear that finding M.C. may mean finding a corpse.

chapters.title: What the Organist Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and organist Theo Brandt's POVs. Theo, Hazel's quiet confidant and growing love interest, admits his predecessor left him a sealed letter naming Judge Aldous Crane as the man who arranged Vane's erasure—and warning him never to open it while Crane lives. The beat: intimacy deepening as trust becomes dangerous.

chapters.title: Ash Wednesday
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A fire guts the archive wing, destroying the ledgers Hazel needs days before the trial. She escapes with one ledger page hidden in her coat but realizes someone inside the cathedral is working against her. The beat: violation and resolve; the sanctuary itself has turned hostile.

chapters.title: The Annuity Trail
chapters.summary: Hazel and Theo's joint POV chapters interleave. Following the annuity payments to a shuttered convent two counties away, they learn 'M.C.'—Miriam Cade—was declared dead on paper but last seen alive by a dying nun who whispers a location: the lighthouse at Grayhaven Point. The beat: hope sharpening into urgency as the trial date looms.

chapters.title: Grayhaven
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the lighthouse Hazel finds Miriam Cade alive, old and bitter, unwilling to testify against Crane—who is her half-brother and the father of the child she lost to his threats. Miriam gives Hazel proof instead: letters implicating Crane in all four deaths. The beat: compassion for a woman broken by duty's opposite—survival over justice.

chapters.title: The Price of the Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Crane discovers Theo's sealed letter and offers him the organist's dream post in exchange for silence; when Theo refuses, he's attacked and hospitalized, and Hazel realizes Crane knows she has the evidence. Torn between staying at Theo's side and protecting Miriam, Hazel chooses duty—with love as the cost. The beat: heartbreak as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Verdict Before the Verdict
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. On trial's eve, Crane corners Hazel in the crypt to bargain for the letters; she stalls him while Marsh records the confession hidden in the founder's empty coffin, where Hazel had staged the exchange. Crane is arrested; the trial collapses into his arraignment. The beat: terror transfigured into triumph, justice seized outside the courtroom.

chapters.title: A Name in the Register
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Hazel enters her own findings officially into the restored archive—the first record bearing her name as investigator rather than keeper. Visiting recovering Theo, she opens the future she'd always deferred. Miriam attends Vane's reburial, finally mourned. The beat: identity claimed, love chosen, silence ended.
